title: Зависть поваров и совет Максу  (The Cooks' Envy and a Tip for Max)

segments.t: After tasting the salad, Senya, Fedya, and Lyova grumble amongst themselves that the young newcomer must have had a rich father help him climb the ladder. Meanwhile, Aleksandr wins Max over by showing him a simple trick to rest meat for two minutes so it cooks much faster.
Ну, я надеюсь, по крайней мере.
Погоди, ты же в метрополе начинал.
После этого ты приготовишь его гораздо быстрее.
Right, let's take their exchange slowly and unpack the Russian.
'This should be delicious.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'this' before landing on 'tasty'.
Ну, я надеюсь, по крайней мере.
'Well, I hope so, at least.' Lyova anchors the line on 'come on', while 'measure' completes the thought.
'Or else his daddy helped him out.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'or' and finishing on 'helped'. Lyova answers right away.
'Just like him.' The grammar packs 'how' and 'him' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Would have achieved something too.' Chef Viktor anchors the line on 'some', while 'achieved' completes the thought.
'I would like to see him try.' The '-l' ending on the verb meaning 'looked' places the action in the masculine past tense. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'Where I started out.' In Russian, the idea of 'where' flows naturally into 'to begin' without extra filler words.
Погоди, ты же в метрополе начинал.
'Hold on, you started out at the Metropol.' Notice how Russian expresses 'wait' and 'to begin' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Oh, right, it was Lyova who started at the Metropol.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'and' before landing on 'Metropol'. Lyova answers right away.
'In order to do that.' The grammar packs 'for' and 'that' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Beforehand.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'before' and finishing on 'that'.
'Let it rest for two minutes.' Lyova brings out the contrast between 'give' and 'to him' in a few short words. Chef Viktor answers right away.
После этого ты приготовишь его гораздо быстрее.
'After that, you will cook it much faster.' The grammar packs 'after' and 'faster' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Now let's listen to the entire scene again without interruption.
